Exact Additive Decomposition of the SCI

Source: R/decompose.R
sci_decompose.Rd

Breaks the reported Submission Confidence Index into the exact points each pillar, and each indicator, earns and leaves on the table, so a single score can be read as a reconciled waterfall rather than a black box. Unlike sci_explain(), which ranks loss contributions using the nominal pillar weights, this decomposition uses the effective weights that compute_sci() actually applied, so the earned points sum back to the reported SCI even when a pillar is missing and its weight has been redistributed.

Usage

sci_decompose(evidence, config = sci_config_default())

Arguments

evidence

A validated evidence data.frame (from r4subcore).

config

An sci_config from sci_config_default(). Pass a profile configuration here for authority-calibrated weights and bands.

Value

A list of class "sci_decomposition" with:

  • sci: the reported SCI (rounded), after any band gate on the score's band (the numeric score itself is never gated)

  • sci_exact: the unrounded weighted sum the earned points reconcile to

  • band: the decision band, including any non-compensatory gate

  • residual: sci - sci_exact, the rounding residual

  • pillars: a tibble with pillar, pillar_score (0–1), nominal_weight, effective_weight, weight_budget, earned, shortfall, and scored

  • indicators: a tibble with indicator_id, indicator_name, indicator_domain, indicator_score, effective_weight, n_in_pillar, earned, and shortfall, ordered by earned descending

Details

The SCI is a weighted average of pillar scores scaled to 0–100:

SCI = sum(effective_weight * pillar_score) * 100

where the effective weights are the nominal config weights renormalised over the pillars that actually have a score (see compute_sci()). This function reuses those exact effective weights rather than recomputing them, so no scoring semantics are introduced or changed here.

For each scored pillar it reports two quantities that partition the pillar's weight budget (effective_weight * 100):

  • earned: the points the pillar contributes to the SCI, effective_weight * pillar_score * 100.

  • shortfall: the points the pillar leaves on the table, effective_weight * (1 - pillar_score) * 100.

earned + shortfall equals the pillar's weight budget, the earned column sums to the (unrounded) SCI, and the shortfall column sums to 100 - SCI.

The same partition is pushed down to indicators. A pillar score is the mean of its k scored indicators, so each scored indicator carries an equal share effective_weight / k of the pillar's budget and earns effective_weight / k * indicator_score * 100. Indicator earned points sum to their pillar's earned points, and therefore to the SCI overall. Pillars and indicators with no score (NA) are reported with NA contributions and are excluded from the sums, exactly as they are excluded from the SCI.

A tiny rounding residual (sci_exact - sci) can arise because the reported SCI is rounded to one decimal place; it is returned as residual and is at most 0.05 in magnitude.

See also

sci_explain() for loss-ranked contributions under nominal weights, indicator_contributions() for remediation headroom, and compute_sci() for the underlying score.

Examples

ctx <- suppressMessages(r4subcore::r4sub_run_context("STUDY1", "DEV"))
ev <- suppressMessages(r4subcore::as_evidence(
  data.frame(
    asset_type = "validation", asset_id = "ADSL",
    source_name = "pinnacle21",
    indicator_id = c("Q1", "Q2", "T1", "R1", "U1"),
    indicator_name = c("Missing var", "Label", "Trace", "Risk", "Guide"),
    indicator_domain = c("quality", "quality", "trace", "risk", "usability"),
    severity = c("high", "low", "medium", "high", "low"),
    result = c("fail", "pass", "warn", "fail", "pass"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  ctx = ctx
))
dec <- sci_decompose(ev)
dec
#> 
#> ── SCI decomposition ──
#> 
#> ℹ SCI 30.6 / 100   Band "high_risk"
#> 
#> ── Pillars (earned / budget) 
#> • quality: 13.12 earned, 21.88 short (of 35)
#> • trace: 6.25 earned, 18.75 short (of 25)
#> • risk: 0 earned, 25 short (of 25)
#> • usability: 11.25 earned, 3.75 short (of 15)
#> 
#> ── Top earning indicators 
#> • Q2 (quality): 13.12 SCI points
#> • U1 (usability): 11.25 SCI points
#> • T1 (trace): 6.25 SCI points
#> • Q1 (quality): 0 SCI points
#> • R1 (risk): 0 SCI points
dec$pillars
#> # A tibble: 4 × 8
#>   pillar    pillar_score nominal_weight effective_weight weight_budget earned
#>   <chr>            <dbl>          <dbl>            <dbl>         <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 quality          0.375           0.35             0.35            35  13.1 
#> 2 trace            0.25            0.25             0.25            25   6.25
#> 3 risk             0               0.25             0.25            25   0   
#> 4 usability        0.75            0.15             0.15            15  11.2 
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: shortfall <dbl>, scored <lgl>
